citation.title: Following the money: trade associations, political activity and climate change
citation.type: journal article (saved SpringerLink landing page: abstract and reference list only)

question: What political activities US trade associations engaged on climate change carry out and spend money on, and what explains the variation in spending (abstract only).
data: Per the abstract: an original dataset built from trade associations' IRS filings, covering 10 years of spending, plus semi-structured interviews. Which filings, which period and how many associations are not stated in the file.
method: Per the abstract: descriptive spending totals, a regression analysis and semi-structured interviews. How associations were selected or classified is not stated in the file.

findings.claim: Trade associations engaged on climate change spent $3.4 billion in 10 years on political activities.
findings.quote: we find that trade associations engaged on climate change spent $3.4 billion in 10 years on political activities

findings.claim: The largest expenditure was on advertising and promotion, followed by lobbying, grants and political contributions.
findings.quote: with the largest expenditure on advertising and promotion, followed by lobbying, grants and political contributions

limitations.point: The file holds only the abstract, the reference list and page furniture from a subscription landing page, not the article text. Nothing on definitions, classification of associations, or method detail could be recorded.
limitations.quote: This is a preview of subscription content, log in via an institution to check access.

limitations.point: The authors say the data files will be made available at publication on request to the lead author; they are not posted with the article.
limitations.quote: The quantitative data files underlying this article will be made publicly available at publication by request to Dr. Robert Brulle.
